claims.text: If you don't know how you can lose money in an opportunity, you will lose money in it, because the unknown ways you can lose reflect how little you actually know about that opportunity.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: lack of prior experience in the domain
claims.mechanism: Absence of identified failure modes is an index of knowledge gaps; those gaps manifest as unanticipated losses.

claims.text: Identify downside in three steps: first, enumerate all the different ways the downside can occur; second, attach a reasonable likelihood to each way; third, multiply your total estimated loss by three to account for optimism bias.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

claims.text: Entrepreneurs have optimism as a quintessential trait, required to start a business, but carrying that same optimism into every new opportunity destroys capital because it prevents clear-eyed downside evaluation.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Optimism bias blinds founders to costs and risks that would be visible to a neutral party; the same trait that enables first action prevents sober opportunity evaluation.
bounded_by: Does not apply to the decision to start a first business, where optimism is constructive.

claims.text: When you split focus across multiple opportunities, you lose the depth of knowledge required to identify all the ways you can lose money in any single one, making capital destruction inevitable.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Shallow knowledge of each opportunity creates blind spots; blind spots compound into unanticipated losses across all opportunities simultaneously.

practices.text: Before entering a new opportunity, write down every plausible way you could lose money, estimate the probability of each, and use that list to decide whether to proceed.
Multiply your initial downside estimate by three to correct for the entrepreneurial optimism bias that systematically underestimates risk in new ventures.
Keep your portfolio of opportunities narrow enough that you maintain expert-level knowledge in each one, so you can identify the hidden costs and failure modes that would otherwise destroy capital.
